topic: Fill in the Blanks (Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension)

sections.title: Basic Concept of Fill in the Blanks
sections.content: In Fill in the Blanks questions, one or more parts of a sentence are left blank. You must choose the correct word or phrase to make the sentence meaningful and grammatically correct. Step 1: Understand the meaning of the entire sentence. Step 2: Identify clue words such as conjunctions or tone indicators. Step 3: Choose a word that fits both the meaning and grammar of the sentence.

sections.title: Phrasal Verbs
sections.content: A phrasal verb = Verb + Preposition/Adverb. Its meaning is often different from the literal meaning of the verb. Step 1: Identify the verb. Step 2: Look at the particle (preposition/adverb) attached to it. Step 3: Understand the meaning of the complete phrasal verb. Example: The meeting was called off due to heavy rain. (call off = cancel)

sections.title: Idioms in Context
sections.content: Idioms are phrases whose meanings are different from the literal meanings of the individual words. Step 1: Understand the tone of the sentence. Step 2: Recall the common meaning of the idiom. Step 3: Choose the idiom that best fits the context. Example: He finally broke the ice during the meeting. (break the ice = start a conversation)

sections.title: Editorial Vocabulary (The Hindu Style)
sections.content: Editorial passages often contain formal vocabulary such as significant, inevitable, crucial, deteriorate, etc. Step 1: Identify the overall tone of the sentence. Step 2: Determine whether the tone is positive or negative. Step 3: Choose vocabulary that matches the context. Example: The policy change had a significant impact on the economy.

sections.title: Contrasting Conjunctions
sections.content: Contrasting conjunctions show opposition between two parts of a sentence. Common words include although, despite, nevertheless, and however. Step 1: Check whether the two clauses show contrast. Step 2: Choose the appropriate connector. Step 3: Verify the grammatical structure. Example: Although he was tired, he continued working.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Choosing a word only based on grammar while ignoring meaning. 2. Taking the literal meaning of a phrasal verb. 3. Not understanding the tone of conjunctions. 4. Getting confused between similar-looking words.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Fill in the Blanks, understanding the context is the most important factor. Identify the correct meanings of phrasal verbs and idioms. In editorial vocabulary, recognize the tone of the sentence, and use contrasting conjunctions to understand the relationship between the two parts of the sentence.

tricks.title: Context First Rule
tricks.explanation: Read the entire sentence first and understand its meaning before filling the blank.
tricks.example: The manager decided to call off the meeting due to rain.

tricks.title: Identify Verb + Particle
tricks.explanation: If you see a verb with a nearby preposition or adverb, think about a phrasal verb.

tricks.title: Tone Detection Trick
tricks.explanation: Identify whether the sentence expresses a positive or negative tone.

tricks.title: Contrast Signal Trick
tricks.explanation: If two parts of the sentence are opposite in meaning, think of words like although, despite, or however.
tricks.example: Although it was raining, they continued the match.

tricks.title: Idiom Memory Trick
tricks.explanation: Memorize common idioms as complete phrases.
tricks.example: Hit the nail on the head = to say something exactly right.

tricks.title: Elimination Method
tricks.explanation: Remove options that do not fit grammatically or logically.
tricks.example: If the sentence is in past tense, eliminate present tense verbs.

tricks.title: Editorial Word Clue
tricks.explanation: Formal passages usually contain formal vocabulary.

tricks.title: Connector Logic Trick
tricks.explanation: Identify the relationship between clauses such as contrast, cause, or result.
tricks.example: He was tired; nevertheless, he finished the work.
